item.title: US Coast Guard says it intercepted ship carrying fuel to Cuba
item.description:
US says ship thought to be using common ‘dark fleet’ tactics was boarded and taken to Mexico as embargo continues

The US Coast ⁠Guard has announced that it intercepted a large cargo ship carrying fuel bound for Cuba, as the ⁠Trump administration’s crippling ⁠oil embargo against ​the island nation continued.

The vessel named Grace was stopped on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba ⁠and Mexico while using tactics to evade authorities, the Coast Guard said. The New York Times reported that the ship ⁠was 91 metres (300ft) long.

Leaders agree a coordinated drawdown after surge in prices and Donald Trump’s threat to cut off US supplies

Leaders of G7 nations are to release up to 100m barrels of their emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off supplies of US diesel.

The French President, Emmanuel Macron, said ministers from some of world’s largest economies had agreed to release stocks from their strategic oil reserves after crisis talks on Friday.

item.title: Suicide by plane or terrorism? Speculation over motive in flight 1073 attack
item.description:
Experts sceptical flydubai co-pilot’s only motivation was to end his own life and say key question is means of radicalisation

At about 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter, Nina, to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.

Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he did not react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.

item.title: Morning recap
item.description:
Morning recap

Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you're just joining us, here are key developments: 

* US President Donald Trump has again said that the war with Iran could end soon, "probably right after the elections", while questioning who in Tehran Washington could negotiate with.

* Trump's top cabinet members met secretly at Camp David on Friday to discuss next steps in the Iran war and the Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen, Axios reported, citing three US officials familiar with the matter.

* Yemen’s armed forces say they carried out 71 attacks targeting Houthi gatherings, reinforcements and military buildups across several areas of Taiz province, Al Jazeera reported.

* The death toll from an Israeli strike on an apartment in Gaza City has risen to five, Palestinian medical sources have told Al Jazeera.

* The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 attempted to carry out a "terrorist" attack during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, according to the state news agency WAM.

* Israeli settlers killed 19-year-old Palestinian Bahaa Sami Amin Nathsheh in Kobar, north of the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, citing the health ministry.

* Debris from a ballistic missile that was shot down in Saudi Arabia's Ahad Rafidah Governorate in the Asir region injured a resident, according to the Saudi Directorate of Civil Defence.

* Two Iranian nationals were charged in Britain with preparing a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in northern England, police said on Friday.

* The master of a crude oil tanker has reported being struck by an unknown projectile 4 nautical miles east of Oman, ⁠according to the United Kingdom ​Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

* Green Party leader Zack Polanski has called for Palestine Action to be de-proscribed, SkyNews reported.

* A source close to the UAE government has accused the Israeli government of exploiting the flydubai incident for political purposes and delaying the restoration of flydubai service, according to Ynet.

* The United States has issued sanctions against three individuals and two France-based charities that it said were part of a network that raised more than $2 million for Hamas, and announced six arrests.

item.title: Trump's top cabinet members discuss Iran, Houthi conflict at Camp David, report says
item.description:
Trump's top cabinet members discuss Iran, Houthi conflict at Camp David, report says

US President Donald Trump's top cabinet members met secretly at Camp David on Friday to discuss next steps in the Iran war and the Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen, Axios reported, citing three US officials familiar with the matter.

Axios said the meeting, chaired by Vice President JD Vance, was not announced by the Trump administration, and the last time a similar meeting took place was in June 2025, just days before Israel went to war against Iran.

Among the other participants were Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, White House envoy Steve Witkoff, CIA director John Ratcliffe and chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff General Dan Caine, the outlet reported.

"Things were decided or at least deeply discussed," one of the officials said, referring to the crisis in the Middle East.

item.title: Yemeni forces claim 71 attacks on Houthi targets in Taiz
item.description:
Yemeni forces claim 71 attacks on Houthi targets in Taiz

Yemen’s armed forces say they carried out 71 attacks targeting Houthi gatherings, reinforcements and military buildups across several areas of Taiz province, Al Jazeera reported.

A Houthi military spokesperson said the operations targeting al-Aqrud, Samea, al-Ahkum, al-Akboush, Jabal Rasin, Jabal Jardad, Bani Omar, Bani Bakari, al-Kaawish and al-Athawir destroyed several Houthi transport and support vehicles and caused casualties among the group’s fighters.

item.title: Crude oil tanker hit by unknown projectile off Oman, UKMTO says
item.description:
Crude oil tanker hit by unknown projectile off Oman, UKMTO says

The master of a crude oil tanker has reported being struck by an unknown projectile 4 nautical miles east of Oman, ⁠according to the United Kingdom ​Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

In a post on X, UKMTO said all crew are reported safe and no environmental impact is currently reported. It advised vessels transit with caution.
